negative_findings.description: English-language search for MK bank vacancies mentioning ISO8583, acquiring or core banking returned no vacancy listings at all — only Wikipedia bank entries and open-banking directories.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero relevant hits; confirms MK payments vacancies are advertised almost exclusively in Macedonian and are invisible to English queries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collection design for this cell must be Macedonian-first; an English-only monitor would report a false null on hiring activity.

negative_findings.description: No MK-language vacancy text encountered in this pass used the term 'ISO8583' or an obvious Macedonian equivalent; MK ads describe the domain functionally ('картично работење', 'банкомати', 'самоуслужни производи') rather than by protocol name.
negative_findings.result_summary: Protocol-level keywords are the wrong filter for MK job text.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A keyword list built from Western payments jargon will miss most MK ads. Filters must use functional Macedonian vocabulary.

negative_findings.description: LinkedIn company pages for MK banks, KIBS and vendors are the single richest indirect signal but are behind an auth wall and covered by ToS prohibiting automated collection.
negative_findings.result_summary: Content exists and is partially visible via search-engine snippets; systematic automated collection is not permissible.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The highest-yield source in this cell cannot be pipelined; budget manual analyst time or an authorised data route instead of assuming a scraper.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated, MK-hosted payments or cards conference (a 'Skopje Payments Summit' equivalent) was identified. MK payments discussion is distributed across e-commerce, ICT-chamber and general business events, or happens at regional events abroad.
negative_findings.result_summary: No standalone national payments conference found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Event monitoring must be multi-venue rather than anchored on one flagship event; absence itself is an intelligence datum about market maturity.

negative_findings.description: No MK bank or vendor career page (kb.com.mk, stb.com.mk, nlb.mk, halkbank.mk, casys.com.mk, kibs.mk) was opened and confirmed in this pass; their existence and URL shape are inferred from third-party references only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Aggregators lag and filter; primary career pages are the authoritative first-publication point and must be enumerated before the collection design is fixed.

negative_findings.description: No specific NBRSM working paper on cash usage, card acceptance or payment habits was located by title in this pass — only the section-level pages that should host such papers.
negative_findings.result_summary: Container located, individual items not enumerated.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The research layer of this cell is asserted at section level only; item-level enumeration is still owed.

negative_findings.description: No Albanian-language (sq) sources were sought or found, despite Albanian being widely used in North Macedonia including by some banks and in Tetovo/Skopje-area universities.
negative_findings.result_summary: sq layer entirely absent from this pass (run scope specified mk+en only).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A meaningful slice of MK job ads, event coverage and university output is Albanian-language and is being systematically missed.

coverage_gaps.description: Primary career pages of the ~13 MK banks, plus CaSys, KIBS, Diners Club MK, Paysera MK and the payment institutions/e-money institutions registered with NBRSM, are not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull the NBRSM registers of banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions and payment system operators, then resolve each entity to its careers URL and LinkedIn page to form a fixed watchlist.

coverage_gaps.description: The MK functional vocabulary for payments roles is only partially assembled (картично работење, платен промет, банкомати, самоуслужни производи, платежни решенија, засилена автентикација).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a full mk keyword set including еквајринг, издавање картички, процесирање, ПОС мрежа, тргoвци, инстант плаќања, СЕПА, отворено банкарство, and their English-in-Macedonian variants, and validate each against real ad text before locking filters.
Add an sq query set (shpallje pune bankë Shkup kartela pagesa; konferencë fintech Shkup) and check South East European University and Mother Teresa University output.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival strategy identified for vacancy text, which is deleted once a post expires — the signal is perishable.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Capture ad full text at discovery time and store it, and check Wayback coverage of bankarstvo.mk and the main job boards to backfill a historical hiring series.

coverage_gaps.description: Event agendas and speaker lists were identified at organiser level but no past-edition agenda was actually retrieved, so the speaker-to-institution map is unbuilt.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the last three editions of the Regional E-commerce Conference and MASIT specialised events; extract speaker names, titles and employers into an actor map.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-side signals for the ATM/POS supply chain (Payten, Printec, Diebold/NCR partners, ASSECO SEE in MK) were not located — the vendor query returned only Nextsense.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted mk+en queries per vendor name plus 'Скопје'/'Македонија', and check the Central Register and public-procurement portal for their MK legal entities and bank contracts.

coverage_gaps.description: LinkedIn — the richest layer — is not lawfully pipelineable, and e-Rabota is an ASP.NET postback form that resists simple crawling.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Design a hybrid: automated collection on open aggregators (bankarstvo.mk, vrabotuvanje, apliciraj), scheduled manual review for LinkedIn, and a session-aware fetcher for e-Rabota.

brief: North Macedonia's weak-signal layer is real but Macedonian-only: English queries for cards/acquiring/ISO8583 vacancies return literally nothing, while the same search in Macedonian ('картично работење', 'платен промет', 'банкомати') surfaces named card-business roles at UNIBanka, TTK, NLB, Sparkasse and Komercijalna within one page of results. The practical backbone is a three-part watchlist: aggregators that republish bank vacancy text in full (bankarstvo.mk, vrabotuvanje.com.mk, apliciraj.mk, the state e-Rabota register), institution-level rosters and agendas (the MBA's Commission for Payment Cards and Digital Banking, which names the cards owner at each major bank; MASIT's specialised SEPA events; the annual Regional E-commerce Conference in Skopje), and the research/award layer (NBRSM working papers, UKIM theses that often reprint primary card and ATM series, and Global Finance / The Banker / EMEA Finance citations that date each bank's digital initiatives). Two structural constraints shape any collection design: LinkedIn holds the densest signal — KIBS, CaSys, Komercijalna, Nextsense all post there — but is auth-walled and ToS-restricted, so it needs analyst time rather than a scraper; and vacancy text is perishable, so ads must be archived at discovery or the historical hiring series is lost. Notable absences worth recording as findings in their own right: no standalone national payments conference exists, MK ads never use protocol jargon like ISO8583, and the Albanian-language layer was out of run scope and is entirely uncovered.
